newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Inquiry ordered into Irish prisoner blunder.
newsitem.headline: Inquiry ordered into Irish prisoner blunder.

text.p: Justice minister Nora Owen apologised in parliament on Thursday for a mix-up which has led to the release of 21 prisoners.
She said that late on Wednesday night the Attorney General had advised that the prisoners had to be released.
They had been sentenced by a panel of three judges which included one who, at his own request, had been relieved of his duties in that court by the government in August.

Judge Dominic Lynch, after years serving in the Special Criminal Court, had asked in July to be relieved of this duty. On August 1 the Government agreed -- but the judge was never told and continued to deal with cases.
Owen said the mix up was now the subject of an inquiry.
She said one of her senior officials became aware on Wednesday that a serious problem had emerged over cases dealt with by the judge.

When the Attorney General advised later that night that the prisoners had to be released, the Director of Public Prosecutions ordered that they all be re-arrested and brought before the Special Criminal Court again, Owen said.
By 0200 GMT on Thursday, 15 prisoners in various jails had been released and immediately re-arrested.

Shortly before lunch on Thursday a sixteenth prisoner was released and re-arrested, and in the afternoon another five prisoners who were dealt with by the same judge since August 1 were given bail by the courts.
The opposition spokesman on justice, John O'Donoghue, called on the Minister to resign.
